deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: This controls whether Terraform is allowed to destroy the attached-disk resource. It falls under the prevent-destructive-loss archetype because a generic platform policy can require deletion protection to prevent accidental destruction of the managed resource.

device_name.description: Specifies a unique device name of your choice that is reflected into the /dev/disk/by-id/google-* tree of a Linux operating system running within the instance. This name can be used to reference the device for mounting, resizing, and so on, from within the instance. If not specified, the server chooses a default device name to apply to this disk, in the form persistent-disks-x, where x is a number assigned by Google Compute Engine.
device_name.rationale: This specifies the guest operating system device identifier used to reference the attached disk. It is an operational naming value inside the guest OS rather than a platform-level security control, so constraining it would not provide a useful generic security policy.

disk.description: name or self_link of the disk that will be attached.
disk.rationale: This identifies the persistent disk resource that will be attached. It is a reference to another resource rather than a security configuration value on this resource, so a generic platform policy should not constrain the specific disk reference.

instance.description: name or self_link of the compute instance that the disk will be attached to. If the self_link is provided then zone and project are extracted from the self link. If only the name is used then zone and project must be defined as properties on the resource or provider.
instance.rationale: This identifies the compute instance to which the disk is attached. It is a reference to another resource rather than a standalone security control, so constraining the specific instance reference would require environment-specific knowledge and is not a useful generic policy target.

interface.description: The disk interface used for attaching this disk. One of SCSI or NVME. (This field is only used for specific cases, please don't specify this field without advice from Google.)
interface.rationale: This selects the disk interface used for the attachment, such as SCSI or NVME. These are functional and architectural configuration options rather than secure versus insecure values, so restricting the interface would not provide a generic security improvement.

mode.description: The mode in which to attach this disk, either READ_WRITE or READ_ONLY. If not specified, the default is to attach the disk in READ_WRITE mode.
mode.rationale: This controls whether the attached disk is accessible in READ_WRITE or READ_ONLY mode. Write access allows the attached instance to modify data, while READ_ONLY limits modification. Because the access mode directly affects the level of access granted to the disk, a generic platform policy can restrict writable attachments where read-only access is required by a security baseline.

project.description: The project that the referenced compute instance is a part of. If instance is referenced by its self_link the project defined in the link will take precedence.
project.rationale: This specifies the project associated with the referenced compute instance. It is an identifier and resource reference rather than a standalone security configuration value, so a generic platform policy should not constrain a specific project ID.

zone.description: The zone that the referenced compute instance is located within. If instance is referenced by its self_link the zone defined in the link will take precedence.
zone.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).
